findings: The adopted September-2026 cohort has 180 credits: sixty in each year. The public generic mobility-window summary cannot replace the actual structured EOR Cluster A requirement. The neutral first non-exchange route is selected independently of UCR fit. Four first-listed Autumn cluster choices and the first Spring choice include BAOR, EME and QFAS. The separate six-credit elective is the first remaining Spring Cluster A choice under the explicit additional-cluster rule, not an unrestricted block.

Fall year three has four cluster units and Philosophy of Science and Statistics, thirty credits. Spring has Auctions, Policy Analysis, Philosophy and History of Economic Thought and the twelve-credit thesis, thirty credits. Probability and Statistics is counted once across two blocks; first-year society-lab activities are zero-credit, with the single six-credit completion in year two. No repeated lab, second philosophy, exchange or additional elective inflates the total.

The thesis is independent EOR research, including critical literature study, research, written English thesis and two mandatory English meetings. EER 4.5.7(iii) explicitly requires 144 credits including ISL for EOR, and the dated thesis entry confirms that minimum before starting. This example reaches 150 credits including ISL before Spring. General 120/138 rules are not substituted. Named specialist course prerequisites and mathematical preparation are supplied in earlier years.

Fifty-three interests have fourteen generators, twenty-five support topics and fourteen search-only examples/outcomes. Eleven direct interests are owned by the closest, including societal quantitative methods concretely addressed through public economics and empirical inquiry. Business analytics and quantitative finance separately produce coherent alternatives. Actuarial science is a separately evidenced candidate at the maximum, not an unsupported academic rejection. No fourth programme is fabricated.

The closest is an academically substantive quantitative economics/econometrics/optimisation response; business analytics emphasises software/data/neural prediction and economic applications; finance emphasises accounting, markets/banking, behavioural choices and quantitative methods. The narrower financial label does not claim a full quantitative-finance or actuarial formation. Pairwise changes of 37.5, 30 and 60 credits each way change content priorities as well as passing the four-course floor.

Thirty-two selected course contributions were reviewed against current evidence. Description-only econometrics explicitly supplies OLS/GLS/IV, tests, Stata simulations and an empirical paper and matches introductory econometrics. Advanced calculus, databases and behavioural economics receive their actual supported scope. Money and Banking offers substantial contracts, markets and bank-risk analysis; Business/AI offers economic and institutional implications. No missing profile is used to reject relevance and no methods beyond descriptions are attributed.

Twenty-one partial relationships and ten dedicated gaps follow actual content. SQL is a specific computational-econometrics module; policy-model/evidence inquiry is shared with Public Economics but Tilburg’s dedicated identification methods are not imported; reasoning biases are an explicit part of Philosophy of Science and Statistics. Numerical ODE/integration is bounded against analytical/measure-theoretic methods. General Ethics is not history of thought, introductory econometrics is not advanced GMM/ML, and insurance, separate games/auctions, society-lab and thesis requirements remain visible. Optional independent research remains additional.

All schedules pass covered offerings, formal prerequisites, twenty-four unique courses/four each semester, first-year PPD and advanced-credit rules. Four original offering conflicts are rescheduled without replacing course selections or restoring historical offerings. Data precedes ML and ML precedes deep learning; methods precedes behavioural statistics/econometrics; algorithms precedes advanced algorithms. Dedicated proof/specialist depth limitations remain explicit.
